protocol.population: Every graph disease and its canonical baseline supported top-k candidates
protocol.group_scope: Every observed BINDS provider label; exact at-most-two label subsets; all compounds jointly reranked
protocol.withdrawal_semantics: Remove union of all BINDS records mentioning any withdrawn label; retain no independent-corroboration assumption
protocol.comparison: Same model and cohort, individual-edge budgets 0..2; scopes differ, so differences are not failed v1.2 guarantees or clinical error rates
protocol.protection: Exact minimum-cardinality additional group conditions; frequency-greedy baseline sees the same full failure family and removes redundant choices
protocol.verification: Every certificate separately recomputed and distinct witnesses replayed with full sparse matrix edits; exact and greedy protection rerun for feasibility
protocol.maximality_oracle: Independent literal-path and all-world enumeration on small graphs in tests/test_provenance_audit.py
protocol.clinical_interpretation: Finite fixed-model sensitivity only; no efficacy, retraction, error probability or prospective savings claim

source.semantics: Exact for this fixed model and the selected provenance-group withdrawal space. Withdrawing a group removes every recorded BINDS edge mentioning that provider label or imported PubMed identifier, including records with other annotations. Overlapping groups remove a record once. An annotation is not proof of independent corroboration, and a PubMed group is not necessarily one experiment. This is a conservative record-quarantine stress scenario, not a factual retraction, clinical effect, or probability of error. All competing compounds change jointly. Protected groups are assumed unavailable for withdrawal; protection does not mean a review or experiment has established that assumption. Binary64 exactness is relative to the declared scorer and numerical runtime; verification rejects numerical mismatches. Other relation families, new records, refitting and unselected groups are outside scope.

certificate.interpretation: Exact for this fixed model and the selected provenance-group withdrawal space. Withdrawing a group removes every recorded BINDS edge mentioning that provider label or imported PubMed identifier, including records with other annotations. Overlapping groups remove a record once. An annotation is not proof of independent corroboration, and a PubMed group is not necessarily one experiment. This is a conservative record-quarantine stress scenario, not a factual retraction, clinical effect, or probability of error. All competing compounds change jointly. Protected groups are assumed unavailable for withdrawal; protection does not mean a review or experiment has established that assumption. Binary64 exactness is relative to the declared scorer and numerical runtime; verification rejects numerical mismatches. Other relation families, new records, refitting and unselected groups are outside scope.
